name: K-Scale Zeroth Bot
description: A small **open-source, 3D-printable humanoid** from **K-Scale Labs**, announced in November 2024 as the **Zeroth-01** after a hackathon project and later sold for pre-order as the **Z-Bot** at **$999**. It has **18 motorised joints**, a **1080p camera**, a dual-core **RISC-V** board, an LED face screen, a microphone and speaker, and a Python SDK with reinforcement-learning walking in simulation. K-Scale Labs **shut down in November 2025**; the designs and code stay public.
sourcing: Verified against the zeroth-robotics GitHub repositories (zeroth-bot and the kscalelabs components), K-Scale Labs' launch post on X, Circuit Digest and Robotic Gizmos write-ups, Interesting Engineering's Z-Bot report, and Mike Kalil's articles on K-Scale's shutdown, as of October 2026. Flagged as uncertain: height, weight and battery capacity were not found; the 18-joint count comes from Circuit Digest (5 per leg, 4 per arm); $350 is a bill-of-materials figure and $999 a pre-order price, so no current price exists; the licence is MIT in the repository while one report says hardware CERN-OHL-S-2.0 and software MIT and also calls them non-commercial, which could not be reconciled; the Discontinued status rests on K-Scale's shutdown, not on a product notice; and the photo is a promotional render with its orange studio background removed.

pricing.summary: There is **no current price** because K-Scale Labs no longer sells the robot. The project repository gives a build cost starting around **$350** for the parts, K-Scale took pre-orders for the Z-Bot at **$999**, and a Kickstarter listing described it as under $1,000. K-Scale cancelled its pre-orders and refunded deposits when it closed. Anyone building one prints the parts and sources the actuators and electronics themselves. robotindex does not sell this product.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: The Zeroth Bot began as a hackathon project at **K-Scale Labs** in 2024 and was announced on 12 November 2024 as the **Zeroth-01**, a roughly $350 DIY humanoid with reinforcement-learning walking, vision, audio and torque-controlled joints. K-Scale later offered it as the **Z-Bot** at $999 alongside its larger **K-Bot** ($8,999), then shut down in **November 2025** after failing to find a lead investor, cancelling pre-orders and refunding deposits. Its founder said the hardware and software for the K-Bot and Zeroth Bot were released publicly, hardware under CERN-OHL-S-2.0 and software under MIT, while the GitHub repository lists an MIT licence and calls the project fully open source; because the sources disagree on whether a non-commercial licence applies, this page carries the **Open Source badge** on the repository's stated licence and flags the discrepancy. This is a different robot from the [Zeroth M1](/product-zeroth-m1), a closed home companion.
